title: Book One · Chapter 52: The Morning at Mr Sun's
story:
Dad takes Ronan past Mr Sun's place on Saturday morning. They are going to buy soap farther along the main road. Mum is working at home.

“There,” Dad says at the second turn.

The repair counter is inside a small shop. There is no sun on the wall. Leo warned Ronan about that. Ronan still looks for one.

A man with short grey hair stands behind the counter. He is reading a note beside a hand tool. Dad greets him as Mr Sun.

Mr Sun looks at Ronan.

“This must be your son.”

“Nearly seven,” Dad says.

“Seven next week,” Ronan corrects him.

“A week matters,” Mr Sun says. “I have work due next week myself.”

He puts the loose hand crank on the counter. Dad examined it on his first visit. Mr Sun points to that same part. Dad found the right problem. But the old part is worn. They cannot use it. Mr Sun needs a new one. Mr Sun told the owner the price. Now Mr Sun is waiting for an answer.

Ronan wants a quick repair from Dad. He watches Dad's hands. Dad has a different question. “Can I try the work here?” he asks. “Just for a few mornings first.”

They talk about a trial. Dad can try the work for three mornings. Mr Sun has enough work for those days. After that, he and Dad can talk again. First they need to agree on the pay. Dad also needs a starting time. “Which tools should I bring?” he asks.

Ronan looks at a row of tins under the counter. Each has a paper name. He understands the names better than the pay talk. Each tin is for one person's things. The names keep the jobs separate.

A customer comes to the counter. Mr Sun needs to serve her now. He cannot finish his talk with Dad. He asks Dad to come back alone on Monday before closing time.

Dad nods and repeats the time. Mr Sun writes it on the back of a plain card. The shop address is on the card, too. Dad can check both the place and time.

Outside, Ronan looks up at Dad. “Do you have the job now?”

“Not yet. We still need to agree on the pay and hours.”

“But he asked you back.”

“Yes. That's a good sign.”

Dad smiles at the invitation to come back. Dad does not call it his new job yet. Ronan puts a small dot for the shop on their map. He marks both turns in the road. Near the counter is a tea shop. It has a red bench outside.

They buy soap. On the way back, they pass another repair shop. Two used bikes stand outside. A man is selling them. Dad remembers his promise about prices. He stops outside with Ronan.

Ronan asks the price of the smaller bicycle. It is much more than four coins. The man lets him stand beside it. But the road is busy. Ronan cannot ride there.

Dad stands beside the bike and checks its wheel. He does not offer to buy the bicycle. Ronan doesn't ask him to.

Back at home, Mum hears about both stops. She asks first about Mr Sun's terms. “We still need to agree on some details,” Dad says. He explains the pay and hours. Then Mum turns to Ronan. “Did the bicycle have a bell?”

“A horrible one,” he says. “It hardly rang.”

“You have a good bell at home,” Dad says.

Ronan smiles. He takes the bell off the shelf and presses it once. The bell makes its bright, clear sound. Ronan smiles and presses it again. His parents did not buy a bike today.

He wraps it loosely again and puts it back. Below the map's new shop dot, he writes MR SUN. Dad puts his card in the family notebook. The notebook holds the card and the time. He will go back on Monday to talk.
studyGuide:
---

重点表达：counter＝柜台；trial＝试工；agree＝商定；worn＝磨损的。

辅助理解：closing time＝关门时间；before closing time＝关门前。

理解问题：

1. Dad 和 Mr Sun 见面时需要商定什么？
2. Ronan 为什么不能把这次谈话当成已经得到稳定工作？
